title: Architecture and Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary
This document captures Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance, and the ADR process. It is intended as the canonical reference for engineers and architects when designing or updating services that interact with the inference platform.

Goals
- Ensure consistent, backward-compatible public APIs for customers and internal services.
- Maintain high reliability and predictable latency for inference workloads.
- Standardize observability and alerting to reduce MTTR.
- Provide clear, audit-friendly infrastructure and security patterns for hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Create an ADR workflow so important decisions are recorded, discoverable, and reversible.

Scope
Applies to all service teams building production components that: handle customer traffic, provide inference endpoints, participate in routing/fallbacks, or integrate with the Console and bookkeeping systems.

1) API Standards
Overview
APIs exposed by Redwood must be consistent, discoverable, and stable. Follow RESTful principles for control plane endpoints and gRPC + HTTP/2 for low-latency internal RPCs where appropriate. Public-facing inference endpoints may remain REST/HTTP/JSON for compatibility.

Design rules
- Versioning: /v{major}/... in the path. Major version increment implies breaking changes. Deprecation lifecycle: announce 90 days, 30-day reminder, 30-day removal for non-critical; 180 days for widely-used features.
- Idempotency: All mutating operations must support idempotency keys.
- Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination (cursor, limit). Responses include next_cursor or null.
- Filtering & Sorting: Use explicit query params (filter_by, sort_by) not ad-hoc search payloads.
- Error model: Standardized error envelope {"code":"STRING_CODE","message":"human message","details":{}}. Use semantic codes (e.g., INVALID_REQUEST, RATE_LIMITED, AUTH_FAILED, BACKEND_ERROR).
- Rate limiting: Tiered rate limits per account and per-route with 429 and Retry-After header. Document limits in API docs per plan.
- Authentication: OAuth2 bearer tokens for platform users and API keys for service-to-service integrations. All tokens rotated via KMS; short-lived service tokens preferred.
- Contract tests: All public APIs must include a contract test suite in CI that runs against a stable test environment.

Example: Inference request (recommended canonical shape)
POST /v1/generate
Request body: {
  "model": "redwood-text-1.0",
  "input": "Translate to French: Hello",
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "stream": false
}
Response: {"id":"req_123","status":"succeeded","outputs":[{"type":"text","text":"Bonjour"}],"cost":{"input_tokens":3,"output_tokens":10}}

Backward compatibility policy
- Additive changes allowed without major bump (new optional fields, new query params).
- Removing fields or changing field types requires major version or explicit migration plan documented in an ADR.

2) Coding Standards
Languages & repositories
- Preferred languages: Go (services & infra controllers), Python (data/ML tooling and evals), TypeScript (frontend/console). Exceptions require architecture approval.
- Monorepos allowed for small teams; cross-team shared libraries live in clearly owned repos with well-defined versioning.

Style & linting
- Use official style guides and linters: gofmt/golangci-lint, black/ruff for Python, ESLint/Prettier for TypeScript. CI must enforce lint passes.

Testing
- Unit tests: target >75% coverage for critical path code.
- Integration tests: exercise service contracts and common failure modes (timeouts, partial failures).
- E2E tests: for release branches, run a minimal smoke test across platform components.
- Golden tests: for model-serving output-sensitive code paths, include deterministic golden sets and stable seeding.

Quality gates & CI
- PRs require two reviewers (at least one from another team) and passing CI.
- Important merges require an approver with ownership tag (CODEOWNERS).

3) Infrastructure Standards
IaC & provisioning
- All cloud resources provisioned via Terraform modules under confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac. Avoid manual console changes; exceptions require RFC and recorded justification.
- Module patterns: resources must include tags {team, env, service, cost_center}.

Networking & security
- VPC design: single VPC per environment with segmented subnets for public, app, and data. Private deployments use mirrored VPCs under customer control.
- Egress policy: default deny; outbound allowed only for required services (NTP, KMS endpoints, container registries).
- Secrets: use cloud KMS/HSM and Vault for short-lived credentials. No secrets in code or in plaintext config.

Capacity & scaling
- Autoscaling: use target tracking policies (CPU, GPU utilization, and custom queue length metrics).
- Reserved capacity: Dedicated offers pinned node groups. Capacity planning doc lives in eng-sre/capacity-planning.

Disaster recovery & backups
- Critical state backups (customer configs, billing data) retained for 90 days with at least daily snapshots. Recovery RTO/RPO targets defined per data class in eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets.

4) Model-Serving Standards
Model packaging & versioning
- Models are published with immutable model IDs: {model-name}@{semver} (e.g., redwood-3b@1.2.0). Metadata includes architecture, tokenizer, KV cache behavior, preferred quantization profiles.
- Store model artifacts in content-addressed artifact registry and record hashes in release metadata.

Serving runtime expectations
- Batching: default continuous batching enabled for low-cost inference. Service owners must define per-route batching policy (max_batch_size, max_wait_ms).
- KV/Prefix caching: endpoints must declare if they use prefix caching; cache keys include model-id + prompt-hash + customer-id.
- Quantization: recommended quantization profiles published in confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Any aggressive quantization that may alter output quality must be gated by regression tests.

Rollouts & fallbacks
- Canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout with health checks at each step (error rate, latency p95).
- Fallback policy: define compatible fallback model(s) in service config; the router performs automatic soft-fallback when capacity or latency SLO at risk.

SLOs for model-serving (example default)
- Latency (inference endpoint, 95th percentile): <= 250ms for small models (<=10B), <= 800ms for large models (>10B) on hosted tier.
- Availability: 99.9% for hosted API; Dedicated SLAs negotiated per contract.
- Correctness: regressions tracked by eval suites; alert on >2% absolute drop on critical prompt sets.

5) Observability Standards
Metrics & instrumentation
- Use OpenTelemetry for traces and metrics. Standard metric prefixes: redwood_<service>_<metric>. Units and labels must be documented in the service-level metrics.md.
- Minimal set for every service: request_count, request_duration_seconds (histogram), request_errors_total, queue_length. For model-serving add tokens_generated_total and kv_cache_hit_ratio.

Tracing & distributed context
- Propagate W3C traceparent and attach route/model metadata to top-level spans. Sample rate: 10% default; increase to 100% for canaries and post-incident capture.

Logging
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, trace_id, user_id (optional), message, attrs. Redact PII and secrets at emission.
- Log retention: 30 days for standard logs, 365 days for audit logs (billing, auth, infra changes).

Dashboards & alerts
- Every service owns a "Service Health" dashboard with: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, traffic, and key business metrics.
- Alerting rules: page-on error rate spike >1% absolute and sustained for 5 minutes or latency p95 exceeding SLO for 10 minutes. Pager duty runbooks must be linked.

6) Performance Standards
Benchmarking & profiling
- Benchmark suite: All model-serving changes must run in eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite using representative workloads (sequence lengths, batch sizes).
- Perf targets: document target p50/p95/p99 for critical flows in the service README.

Optimization guidance
- Kernel selection: runtime picks kernels based on sequence length distribution; teams should expose realistic traffic profiles (histograms) to the runtime during onboarding.
- Batching & caching knobs: tune max_batch_size and max_wait_ms before changing hardware. Prefer CPU/GPU utilization targets (e.g., GPU util 60-80%) to maximize efficiency while meeting latency SLOs.

Cost monitoring
- Track cost-per-token and cost-per-request in Console. Teams should set budgets and alerts if cost exceeds forecast by >15% month-over-month.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)
Purpose
- ADRs make architectural trade-offs explicit, provide context for future engineers, and record alternatives and consequences.

ADR template (required fields)
1. Title (short)
2. Status (proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated)
3. Context (what problem)
4. Decision (what we decided)
5. Consequences (pros/cons, migration plan)
6. Authors and reviewers
7. Date

ADR process
- Create ADR as part of a PR in confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records (markdown saved also in the service repo under docs/adr/).
- Reviewers: include owner_team and at least one cross-team reviewer.
- Accepted ADRs must have an implementation issue (link) and a migration/rollout checklist.

Example ADRs to be created
- Standardize model ID format (e.g., model@semver)
- API major-versioning policy and deprecation windows
- Default tracing sample rate for platform services

Operationalizing and governance
Ownership & updates
- Each service must have an identified architecture owner (CODEOWNERS). Architecture team performs quarterly audits of compliance with these standards.

Exceptions & change control
- Exceptions must be documented as RFCs and linked to a temporary exemption ADR with explicit expiry. Long-term exceptions require sponsorship and an approved mitigation plan.

Appendix: Quick checklists
API checklist:
- [ ] Path uses /v{major}/
- [ ] Contract tests in CI
- [ ] Idempotency supported where appropriate
- [ ] Error envelope and semantic codes used

Model-serving checklist:
- [ ] Model artifact hashed and registered
- [ ] Batching and cache config defined
- [ ] Canary rollout plan and fallback configured
- [ ] Regression evals included

Observability checklist:
- [ ] OpenTelemetry instrumentation present
- [ ] Service Health dashboard exists
- [ ] Alerts and PagerDuty runbooks linked

References and links
- Confluence: eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture (runtime architecture)
- Confluence: eng-infra/terraform-and-iac (IaC guidelines)
- Confluence: applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles

Contact & ownership
For questions about these standards or to request exceptions, contact the Architecture Standards Working Group: architecture-standards@redwood.example.com.
